_gates_comment: NOT documentation. scripts/gate_count_check.js parses scripts.test below, counts the node invocations and the subset that reads 4/, and FAILS THE BUILD if either number here disagrees. scripts/qa/gate_ceiling_check.mjs fails the build if total > ceiling — see docs/GATE-RETIREMENT.md. Update these in the same edit that adds or removes a gate.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_03a: 111 -> 112, deliberately, for receipt_version_is_identity_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the NINTH raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys: the two Glass receipts are the only things that can answer 'is a republish safe?', and on 2026-09-02 BOTH of them held a clock in a field named artifactVersion -- LAST-HARVEST 2026-09-02T21:55:24.391Z, LAST-PUBLISH version=2026-09-02T22:06:23.279Z, the second eleven minutes after that same file held the real id 1788386140-0fbe. Wyatt's words are on that page and nowhere else, and a comparison against a timestamp says 'unchanged' at the exact moment he has written something -- his page's generatedAt moves when a SESSION regenerates it and never when HE saves into it, proven on two real versions (1788385436-4b8b and 1788385523-b046) that carry the identical generatedAt while only the second holds his Google Analytics idea. It also broke a working detector: telling HIS save from a session's publish meant comparing LAST-PUBLISH against the version the notification announced, and two different KINDS of value cannot be compared at all. THE REASON NOTHING CAUGHT IT IS THE REUSABLE HALF: glass_harvest_hook_check.mjs asserts, with a source regex, that the writer stores something under the name artifactVersion, and the runbook reads the same name -- A GATE ON A FIELD'S NAME IS NOT A GATE ON ITS CONTENTS, and the right name is precisely what kept everyone confident. RED-PROOFED ON THE REAL EVENT, NOT A FIXTURE: the two strings above, run through both writers in a sandbox, 9 failures before the fix and 0 after; plus the live-file reader proven able to CONDEMN the receipts as they actually stood that day, so case 7b cannot degrade into agreeing with whatever is on disk; plus a good publish receipt whose own written-at field is a timestamp proven NOT condemned, so the reader is judging the version and not the line. AND ONE THING IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, held by case 5: it refuses a clock and only a clock, and merely WARNS on a value it does not recognise. A strict allow-list on the platform's current <epoch>-<hash> shape would make the harvest stamp start failing the day that format changes, and the harvest hook would then deny every Glass publish -- wedging the one surface Wyatt steers from, to prevent a fault that has never happened.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02i: 110 -> 111, deliberately, for answered_question_retired_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the EIGHTH raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys, in his words at 6:57 PM ET on the day it was written: 'the page continues to re-show me thw e questions AFTER they're harvested. this is NOT fixed and it is a PRIORITY more than any of the SEO work.' SIX TIMES IN TWELVE HOURS his Glass asked him a question he had already answered, and three of those were repaired by hand. The cause is one sentence: harvesting his answer WRITES the ruling and DELETES NOTHING, so the row goes on rendering in Your Call -- two acts joined by a session remembering the second, which is rule 23's forbidden shape. The 22:5xZ harvest is the proof a runbook step cannot carry this: its own commit says 'all five rules-page questions in the Your Call table above are now answered' and it left all five asking, because its mandate was harvest-and-publish. It detected the exact condition and had no authority to act. The gate is the half nobody has to remember, and it also guards the JOIN the retirement acts on -- two sibling questions used to collide onto one id, so his answer to one would have retired the other and the record would have shown him answering a question he never saw. RED-PROOFED ON THE REAL EVENT, NOT A FIXTURE: his five 6:50 PM rules-page questions, verbatim out of commit cb7cfc89 and checked against that commit by the gate itself, replayed against the five keys .planning/wyclau/LAST-HARVEST really stored his answers under -- all 5 caught. Plus: retire_answered.mjs run end to end on his real question (leaves Your Call, his words land in RULED under the qid), the same fixture proven red before the script runs, an unknown id and a missing verdict both refused without writing, and the derived-slug fallback proven still to reproduce all five of his real stored keys character for character -- the line that would orphan every ruling he has ever made if somebody tidied it.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02h: 109 -> 110, deliberately, for sitemap_lastmod_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the SEVENTH raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys, in his words: 'DERIVE the dates, do not hand-type them -- an inaccurate lastmod gets discounted by Google, and a hand-typed date is wrong the moment work continues.' Removing <changefreq> and <priority> is a one-line edit that stays done and needs no gate; a <lastmod> is a CLAIM ABOUT A FILE THAT CHANGES, and on this branch index.html is committed most days, so a date typed today is wrong tomorrow. The failure is silent on both sides -- Google's answer to a sitemap it can prove stale is to quietly discount the dates, and nothing on our side ever observes that. This gate recomputes every date with the exact command he named (git log -1 --format=%cs) rather than holding a copy of the answer, maps each <loc> to its file through CNAME so a page added tomorrow is covered the moment it is listed, and REFUSES rather than substitutes on the three ways a sitemap lies quietly (a loc that resolves to no file, a page git has never committed, a loc on another origin). Red-proofed by hand-typing 2026-08-14 into the live file: caught, named, and told which command fixes it.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02g: 108 -> 109, deliberately, for do_now_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the SIXTH raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys, in his words: 'Do Now: in the Glass, Add a DO now button next to Send to the Chart button that tells RANK to put this task at the top.' He had to type DO NOW in prose BECAUSE that button did not exist, and the request for it then sank to 31 of 39 on his own list -- the feature is its own acceptance test. This gate walks the whole chain end to end on fixtures: a pinned row ranks first over a row RANK was already putting above it; pinning moves ONE row and re-orders nothing else; a second pin releases the first in the same act, so his one interrupt slot can never become a backlog; two pins arriving by hand FAIL the build naming both; a pin on a handle no open row carries is refused rather than vanishing; and the pin is visible both on the Ideas list the moment he taps and on the Tasks card once a session has carried it over. Red-proofed by deleting the pinned-idea rendering, which also caught one of this gate's own assertions being unable to fail (it keyed on `i.now`, a string that also appears in the code that RELEASES pins).
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02f: 107 -> 108, deliberately, for glass_calm_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the FIFTH raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys, in his words: 'the glass looks chaotic again.' Three faults, and all three are this page's one recurring shape -- it says something that is not true, or says it in a way he cannot use. It showed him a filing handle and a raw ISO timestamp instead of the work being done; it carried two status lines, the second apologising for the first, where he asked for one bar with fewer words; and it printed a red 'this page could not read part of BLOCKED ON WYATT' warning above his real decisions, whose cause was the paragraph in that section forbidding paragraphs. The gate holds each to the LIE it could become: the in-hand line must print an OLD marker's words rather than blank, must age and go COLD in his browser rather than at publish, and the warning must go quiet because there is nothing to find -- case 9 proves real prose still raises it, so the fix cannot degrade into blindness. Case 10 fences the writer against the real .planning/CHART.md, which is the only reason any of this was visible: five prose blocks were sitting in that section on a tree where npm test was green. Red-proofed twice on the real file, once for the prose and once when quoting his own words containing an arrow closed the HTML comment early and put six lines back.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02e: 106 -> 107, deliberately, for glass_his_five_asks_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the FOURTH raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys, in his words: 'claude my friend, you just HAVE to fix the glass.' The Glass is the ONE surface he steers this project from, and every fault he listed is the same shape -- the page saying something that is not true. It showed a finished item as if it were in hand; it presented a frozen number as current; it would have hidden a real question written as prose the moment the empty-card fix landed; and it cut his own note in half at a build stamp because a version number's dot was read as a full stop. This gate holds all five to the LIE each could become, not merely to the feature being present -- the in-hand line must go quiet when the close gate writes its line, a missing ledger must render unreadable rather than a confident 'nothing in hand', and the de-shouting must not eat an acronym or a row handle. Red-proofed by gutting the blindness clause.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02d: 105 -> 106, deliberately, for detached_trial_windowless_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the third raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys: Wyatt saw a black node.exe console appear on the Blade and asked what it was -- it is a sea trial, and its X kills an 85-minute run silently. Measured cause (INBOX-20260901T1440Z, and NOT the one that entry guessed): a detached process has no console at all, so on Windows every console child it spawns is given a BRAND-NEW console, which is a visible window. The gate proves the fix BOTH ways on Windows -- a child spawned without windowsHide must show a visible window, or the check declares itself blind rather than passing -- and derives its coverage half by scanning sea_trial.mjs, so a spawn site added next month fails the build instead of opening a window next release.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02c: 104 -> 105, deliberately, for display_size_reads_every_picture_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs again offers ZERO retirement candidates (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys, measured the day it was written: the resize measurement's own size reader handled PNG and JPEG only, so when ~200 files were renamed to .webp the report loop's `if (!nat) continue;` DROPPED 53 files, 2.09 MB -- more than half the library, the board included -- out of .planning/ASSET-DISPLAY-SIZES.md, in silence, while the file kept its heading. Not listed as unmeasured. Absent. This gate fails the build the next time a format arrives that the reader cannot read, and it is red-proofed by deleting the WebP branch from scripts/lib/imagesize.mjs.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02b: 103 -> 104, deliberately, for preload_covers_css_art_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs still offers no retirement candidate, so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys: art named ONLY in a CSS url() is invisible to sharedAssetUrls() BY CONSTRUCTION -- no care inside that function could ever cover it -- and the storm's rain texture was in exactly that state until 2026-09-02, fetched only when the first storm began. This is the one gate in the suite that can see a picture no JavaScript constant names, and it is red-proofed by removing the derivation it guards.
_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02: 100 -> 102, deliberately, for chart_sweep_conserves_check.mjs and glass_done_today_check.mjs. The alternative the ceiling offers is retiring a quiet per-bug gate, and quiet_gate_report.mjs found ZERO candidates: all 18 were touched within 5 days and every one guards a defect a player can see. Trading one of those for a planning-tooling gate is the wrong trade and was refused rather than fudged. What the two buy: SWEEP is now the only thing in this system that DELETES from the document Wyatt reads, and the number at the top of his page changed source. A rewrite that loses a row is unrecoverable, and a count that silently reads 0 is how the last one went wrong.
_assets_comment: INBOX-20260901T1335Z (Wyatt, launch critical): the art was 17.79 MB and every byte of it is on the boot path now that preloadAssets() warms the recipe and badge families. scripts/qa/asset_weight_check.mjs fails the build when assets/ grows past ceilingBytes. Raising it is allowed; raising it without saying in the commit what a player gets for the weight is what this stops. THE CEILING IS SET AT THE CURRENT TOTAL, NOT ABOVE IT -- it sat at 11.00 MB against a 10.57 MB tree until 2026-09-02, which is 0.43 MB of drift the gate could not see. It is now the exact byte total the gate itself prints, so ratcheting it after a compression pass is a copy, not a count.
